description:
FILED s417 (Fable), found while probing the #399 `class Foo;` must-not-fire
cases.  PRE-EXISTING and unrelated to that change (it is the same before and
after).

    sub class { print "mysub(@_)\n"; 7 }
    class Foo;
    print "after\n";

    perl:  mysub(Foo)        <- Foo is a bareword STRING argument
           after
    PCL:   crash â "The function main::pl-Foo is undefined"

PCL emits `(pl-class (p-list-ctx (pl-Foo)))`: it correctly reads `class` as
the user's sub, then wrongly reads its bareword ARGUMENT as another call.

This is the #266 family ("a bare NAME is a CALL only where it is CALLABLE"),
and the reason it is missed is visible in handle_subcalls (~PExpr.pm 4158):
the string reading is chosen from `$prev_is_unary` / `$prev_is_value_op` /
`$prev_is_separator`, all of which require the PREVIOUS token to be an
OPERATOR.  Here the previous token is a WORD (the sub being called), so none
of them is set and the word stays a funcall.

CARE REQUIRED â this is exactly the position #266 deliberately did NOT widen.
Its note says an ABSENCE of knowledge must keep answering CALL, because
widening turned `next`, `goto again` and File::Spec's `curdir` into strings.
The difference here is that there IS knowledge: the previous token is a word
this document knows is a paren-less sub call, so its bareword argument is an
argument, not a call â but `f g` where BOTH are subs is a real nested call, so
the discriminator has to be "is `Foo` callable here?", not the position.

BAR: the s372 gate-SET scan over both populations (this widens what a
classifier sees), plus probes for the shapes that must not move â `f g` with
both declared, `print "x=", nosuch`, `next`, `goto LABEL`, a class-name
invocant, and a bareword filehandle.
subject: A bareword argument to a paren-less user sub call is emitted as a CALL and crashes: `sub class {â¦} class Foo;` dies on undefined pl-Foo
